https://github.com/py-libhdate/py-libhdate/compare/v0.11.1...v1.0.3

Holiday sensor:
- In Israel, "Simchat Torah" is now "Shmini Atzeret, Simchat Torah"
- In Israel, the 30th of Shvat returns "Family Day, Rosh Chodesh"
- The type id has been removed from the state attribute. Use the type if needed.

The above might break an automation that looks at the value of the holiday state, for one of these days.

issue_context.title: Jewish Calendar with latest 2024.12.5 error
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Logs showing repeating error (attached).
I've never had this error before & assume it to be linked to the breaking change mentioned in the 2024.12.5 [announcement ](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2024/12/04/release-202412/#backward-incompatible-changes)concerning “Chanukah, Rosh Chodesh”.

PLEASE NOTE I HAVE NO AUTOMATIONS THAT USE THE HOLIDAY SENSOR!

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.12.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

jewish_calendar

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/jewish_calendar/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant
Source: components/sensor/__init__.py:651
First occurred: 4:49:13 PM (584 occurrences)
Last logged: 9:40:10 PM

Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved (None)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 1065, in _async_update_entity_states
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 978, in async_update_ha_state
    self._async_write_ha_state()
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1148, in _async_write_ha_state
    self.__async_calculate_state()
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1085, in __async_calculate_state
    state = self._stringify_state(available)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1029, in _stringify_state
    if (state := self.state) is None:
                 ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/sensor/__init__.py", line 651, in state
    raise ValueError(
    ...<2 lines>...
    )
ValueError: Sensor sensor.jewish_calendar_holiday provides state value 'חנוכה, ראש חודש', which is not in the list of options provided
```


### Additional information

My analysis suggests, that the breaking change was not committed/corrected to the Hebrew language only to the English one.

Went looking for the available attributes & found all listed in Hebrew without "ראש חודש, חנוכה" but with "Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah" added at the end. So I believe this would support my above analysis.

I then decided to find where I could set the Language for the `jewish_calendar` integration & to my amazement found there is none at all. It used to be in the `configuration.yaml` but that was obviously removed with the move some time ago of having it setup as a regular integration (GUI). How does one do that now? Maybe only at the time of adding the integration?

For now I've switched off the `jewish_calendar_holiday` as it causes an error every minute!

Edit: As I suspected with the configuration settings. [Here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/119412#issuecomment-2167220167).

Oops, yes. I discovered this bug about a week ago but didn't realize it would propagate as such.
This will only happen if the language is set to English, and will obviously not be a problem two days from now (post-rosh chodesh). Obviously this won't be fixed within 2 days, but I will release an update to fix it for a future release.

I get an error message every 30-40 seconds in my logs -- really cluttering them up...

Also just wanted to thank you for an awesome integration - it is not easy to deal with a totally different calendric ecosystem. Much appreciated & thanks.
